name: Web Plura Agency Reports – Client Reports & Site Maintenance Audits
author: Web Plura

sections.description:
Client reporting should not require rebuilding the same WordPress site audit from screenshots, update notes, and scattered checklist items every month.

Web Plura Agency Reports is a WordPress client report, site audit report, and maintenance report builder for agencies, freelancers, and site maintainers who need a clear local handoff from wp-admin.

Use it to create a client-ready WordPress maintenance report before a monthly update, support handoff, WooCommerce review, or care-plan check-in. The report summarizes local site signals that clients can understand: site health, update context, security posture, backup tool visibility, HTTPS status, and WooCommerce presence when WooCommerce is active.

This version runs locally in the WordPress admin. It does not email reports, collect client records, track visitors, require an external account, restrict local report features, or transmit report data externally.

Product page: https://wplura.com/products/web-plura-agency-reports
Terms: https://wplura.com/terms
Privacy: https://wplura.com/privacy

Client Report Features

Agency reporting problems it helps with

Use the free plugin when you need a manual single-site report for:

  • Monthly WordPress maintenance report handoffs for care-plan clients.
  • Pre-update or post-update site audit notes before a client review.
  • Support handoff reports that explain local site health, update context, HTTPS status, backup tool visibility, and WooCommerce presence.
  • Agency-branded report output with a client label, intro message, closing message, and custom work notes.
  • Print-ready reviews, browser PDF saving, and downloadable HTML export without setting up email delivery.

  • Local report history for recent refresh and export events without external report transmission.

  • Manual single-site WordPress client report.

  • Site audit summary for WordPress version, PHP version, updates, HTTPS, and visible site health signals.
  • Maintenance report sections for basic security posture and backup tool visibility.
  • WooCommerce summary when WooCommerce is active.
  • Agency display name for local report branding.
  • Optional local logo attachment ID, client display label, intro message, closing message, and custom work notes.
  • Local section controls and report template presets.
  • Print-ready admin view and downloadable HTML report.
  • Bounded local history for recent report refresh and HTML export events.

Good Fit For

  • Agencies preparing WordPress maintenance reports for care-plan clients.
  • Freelancers documenting pre-update, post-update, or support handoff findings.
  • Site maintainers who need a local HTML report before a client review.
  • WooCommerce site owners who want store presence included in a broader site audit summary.

Privacy

Agency Reports stores a bounded local report transient, a last report timestamp, bounded local report history, local section preferences, and optional report profile fields in WordPress. Optional profile fields include agency name, logo attachment ID, client display label, intro message, closing message, and custom work notes. Report output is limited to local site configuration signals such as WordPress version, PHP version, update counts, HTTPS status, backup tool presence, WooCommerce presence, and administrator-entered report notes.

The plugin does not store client contacts, email recipients, visitor personal data, passwords, secrets, analytics identifiers, or customer records. It does not email reports or transmit report data externally in this local version.

Uninstalling the plugin deletes its local options and transient.

Admin menu counters may show locally cached actionable findings or jobs. Counters are local-only and do not trigger scans, external calls, tracking, or feature restrictions during menu rendering.

Automatic update checks use WordPress.org for public packages.

External Services

This local version does not connect to external services and does not transmit report data externally.

The plugin reads local WordPress configuration, site health signals, update counts, HTTPS status, backup tool presence, and WooCommerce presence. Reports are viewed or exported manually by the administrator. No client contacts, email recipients, visitor personal data, passwords, secrets, analytics identifiers, or customer records are sent externally.

Terms of Service: https://wplura.com/terms
Privacy Policy: https://wplura.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Upload the web-plura-agency-reports folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install the plugin ZIP in wp-admin.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Open Agency Reports in the WordPress admin sidebar.
  4. Set the agency display name if desired, then refresh the local report.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin send reports to clients?

No. This local version provides a manual report view and downloadable HTML report only.

Can I save the report as a PDF?

Yes. Use the Print or save PDF button and your browser’s PDF save option.

Does this plugin require an external account?

No. This local version has no external account dependency and does not transmit report data.

Is this a WordPress client report plugin for agencies?

Yes. It is built for manual single-site client reports, maintenance summaries, local profile fields, section controls, print output, and downloadable HTML handoff reports.

Can I use it for monthly WordPress maintenance reports?

Yes. It helps prepare manual maintenance report handoffs with site audit signals, update context, backup tool visibility, WooCommerce presence when active, and custom work notes.

Does it create automatic scheduled client reports?

No. This free plugin focuses on manual local report creation and export from wp-admin.

Does it monitor multiple client sites from one dashboard?

No. This free plugin builds a local report for the WordPress site where it is installed. It does not provide hosted multi-site monitoring or remote portfolio reporting.

Does it store client email addresses or customer records?

No. It does not store client contacts, email recipients, visitor personal data, analytics identifiers, or customer records.
sections.changelog:
0.1.8

  • Refreshed the WordPress.org readme for clearer agency maintenance report, site audit, client report, and local export search intent.

0.1.7

  • Renamed the plugin display name to Web Plura Agency Reports.

0.1.6

  • Cleaned public package copy so the WordPress.org ZIP presents this plugin as a local base package only.
  • Kept local report refresh, profile settings, section controls, print/PDF, HTML export, and bounded local history available without any paid access check or external service dependency.

0.1.5

  • Removed commercial prompts and service-specific extension naming from the free package so the WordPress.org ZIP remains a strictly local base plugin.
  • Kept local report refresh, profile settings, section controls, print/PDF, HTML export, and bounded local history available without any paid access check or external service dependency.

0.1.4

  • Added a reversible dashboard delivery/history extension surface while local report history remains available.

0.1.3

  • Added a reversible dashboard workflow extension surface while the local Free fallback remains available.

0.1.1

  • Added local report profile fields, section controls, custom work notes, AJAX-first admin saves, branded HTML export, and bounded local report history.
  • Refined the admin dashboard presentation to match the Web Plura Diagnostics WordPress-native UI pattern.
  • Improved summary cards, report section cards, local-only notice, spacing, focus states, and light admin readability.
  • Added native WordPress heading, description, divider, and postbox markup for a more consistent wp-admin presentation.
  • Added contextual WordPress Help Tabs while keeping local manual reports free and local-only.

0.1.0

  • Initial local Agency Reports scaffold with manual single-site report, agency display name, and HTML export.
